summary.text: Feathers are growths of the outer skin that form a bird's plumage, and they are the most complex skin structures found in vertebrates.
They help birds fly, keep warm and stay dry, and their colours help with communication and protection.
A vaned feather has a central shaft with branching barbs, and the barbs' own branches, called barbules, have tiny hooks that link them, while fluffy down lacks the hooks, so it traps air.

facts.label: Made of
facts.value: Keratin proteins, formed in tiny skin follicles

facts.label: Two basic types
facts.value: Vaned feathers outside, down feathers underneath

facts.label: Key flight feathers
facts.value: Remiges on the wings, rectrices on the tail

facts.label: Weight surprise
facts.value: Plumage can weigh two or three times the skeleton

items.prompt: A winter coat is stuffed with down rather than flat contour feathers. Why does down insulate so well?

options.label: Its barbules float free, so it fluffs up and traps air
Its hooks lock tightly into a dense windproof sheet
Its thick central shaft stores warmth from the body
Its stiff vanes hold heat against the skin

items.explain: Down feathers lack barbicels, so the barbules float free of each other, allowing the down to trap air and give excellent thermal insulation.

items.prompt: A bird's feathers together can outweigh its bones. Why are the bones so light?

options.label: They are built mostly from the same keratin as feathers
Many are hollow and contain air sacs
They are replaced by cartilage as the bird matures
They are thin because the feathers carry the load

items.explain: A bird's plumage weighs two or three times more than its skeleton, since many bones are hollow and contain air sacs.

items.prompt: Bare skin is rarely visible under a bird's plumage. Do feathers sprout from all of its skin?

options.label: Yes, they grow from every follicle equally
Yes, but only the down feathers cover it all
No, they arise only from certain well-defined tracts
No, they grow only from the wings and tail

items.explain: Although feathers cover most of the bird's body, they arise only from certain well-defined tracts on the skin.

items.prompt: Why might the colours of a bird that hunts match its habitat?

options.label: They help hide it from its prey, as well as from its own predators
Matching colours only matter to birds that attract mates
Predators ignore camouflage, so only prey birds need it
Colour has no role in how birds blend in

items.explain: Colour patterns act as camouflage against predators for birds in their habitats and also for predators looking for a meal.

items.prompt: A bird pulls feathers from its own body and tucks them into its nest. What do they do there?

options.label: They hide the nest from predators
They protect the eggs from parasites
They keep rivals away from the nest
They insulate the eggs and the young

items.explain: Feathers may be plucked to line the nest and provide insulation to the eggs and young.

items.prompt: Early writing pens were cut from large feathers. Which word is the word "pen" itself descended from?

options.label: The Old English word for a sharp point
A Greek word meaning ink
The Latin word penna, meaning feather
A Germanic word for a reed

items.explain: Quills were early pens made from feathers, and the word pen is derived from the Latin penna, meaning feather.
